en_title: Sony Squashes $2.6 Billion Lawsuit That Claimed It Ran a 'Near Monopoly' and PlayStation Game Prices Were Too High
cn_title: 索尼击退26亿美元诉讼，该诉讼称其拥有「近乎垄断地位」且PlayStation游戏价格过高
opus_summary: 英国消费者权益活动人士Alex Neil提起集体诉讼，指控索尼凭借PlayStation Store的30%抽成向用户收取过高费用，并称其近乎垄断。伦敦竞争上诉法庭驳回诉讼，认为尚未证明PlayStation违反反竞争法。

paragraphs.en: Sony has fought off a legal challenge over the pricing of PlayStation games that argued the company charged "excessive and unfair prices."
paragraphs.cn: 索尼击退了一项针对PlayStation游戏定价的法律诉讼。该诉讼称，索尼收取了「过高且不公平的价格」。

paragraphs.en: The class action lawsuit, filed in the U.K. earlier this year by consumer rights campaigner Alex Neil, claimed that PlayStation had overcharged customers due to its 30% cut of all digital games and add-ons — essentially, anything sold via the PlayStation Store.
paragraphs.cn: 这起集体诉讼由消费者权益倡导者Alex Neil于今年早些时候在英国提起。诉讼称，PlayStation对所有数字游戏和附加内容——基本上也就是通过PlayStation Store销售的所有商品——抽取30%的分成，导致向消费者收费过高。

paragraphs.en: The legal action suggested that Sony's pricing was unfair and its profit margins were excessive. Additionally, it was claimed that PlayStation held a "near monopoly" on video games — in particular, that it forced users to buy from its own digital store rather than offering a range of alternatives.
paragraphs.cn: 诉讼指出，索尼的定价不公平，其利润率过高。此外，诉讼还声称PlayStation在电子游戏领域拥有「近乎垄断地位」——尤其是它迫使用户从其自有数字商店购买，而不是提供多种其他选择。

paragraphs.en: As reported by The Game Business , London's Competition Appeal Tribunal has now tossed out the lawsuit, on the grounds that PlayStation had not been proven to have broken anti-competition laws.
paragraphs.cn: 据The Game Business报道，伦敦竞争上诉法庭现已驳回这起诉讼，理由是没有证据证明PlayStation违反了反竞争法。

paragraphs.en: If successful, the court case would have seen an estimated 12.2 million PlayStation owners in the U.K. compensated for a decade of purchases, amounting to around $215 per person.
paragraphs.cn: 如果诉讼成功，英国估计将有1220万名PlayStation用户因过去十年的购买行为获得赔偿，每人约215美元。

paragraphs.en: In more detail, the new ruling noted that video game fans had a choice of where to play video games — on rival consoles, PC and elsewhere — and that physical games were also currently an option. (It'll be interesting to see how that changes in future.)
paragraphs.cn: 具体来说，新裁决指出，电子游戏爱好者可以选择在哪里玩游戏——在竞争对手的游戏机、PC及其他平台上——而且目前实体游戏也是一种选择。（未来这一情况会如何变化，值得关注。）

paragraphs.en: Because of this, PlayStation was under no obligation to invite third-party stores onto its platform, the tribunal decided, as Sony was just one player in a larger market. Finally, it was agreed that Sony's decision to sell consoles relatively cheaply (compared to their actual cost) indicated that the company was not trying to fleece customers unfairly, even if prices were rising.
paragraphs.cn: 因此，法庭裁定PlayStation没有义务邀请第三方商店入驻其平台，因为索尼只是更大市场中的一个参与者。最后，法庭认定，索尼决定以相对较低的价格销售游戏机（与其实际成本相比），表明即使价格正在上涨，该公司也没有试图不公平地盘剥消费者。

paragraphs.en: Of course, Sony's 30% cut of digital purchases is standard across the industry, with Nintendo, Microsoft and Steam believed to operate similarly. And while PlayStation console prices have risen, the same could be said for all other console manufacturers too, due to factors largely beyond their control.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，索尼对数字购买收取30%的分成是整个行业的标准做法，任天堂、微软和Steam被认为也采用类似的运营方式。虽然PlayStation游戏机的价格上涨了，但由于主要是它们无法控制的因素，所有其他游戏机制造商的价格也同样上涨了。

paragraphs.en: That said, PlayStation could hardly be argued to be struggling financially right now. Sony announced that PS5 had passed the 100 million consoles sold milestone only last week, and that's before the impending arrival of GTA 6 .
paragraphs.cn: 话虽如此，很难说PlayStation目前正面临财务困境。索尼上周才宣布PS5销量已突破1亿台大关，而这还是在即将到来的《GTA6》发售之前。
